user_input: As a Constitutional Law Scholar analyzing the provisions and practical applications of constitutional law regarding state governance and executive roles, please explain how the definitions provided in Article 366 of the Indian Constitution, particularly the definition of "State," are relevant to understanding the scope of disqualifications for membership of a State Legislative Assembly or Council as outlined in Article 191, and how the procedural regulation of financial business by Parliament under Article 119 relates to the legislative powers mentioned in these articles.
reference: Article 366 of the Indian Constitution provides definitions for key expressions used within the Constitution. Specifically, sub-clause (26B) defines "State" for the purposes of articles including 246A, 268, 269, 269A, and 279A, and includes a Union territory with Legislature within this definition. This definition is foundational for interpreting other constitutional provisions. Article 191 outlines the disqualifications for membership of the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council of a State. Clause (1)(a) specifies a disqualification if a person holds any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State specified in the First Schedule. The definition of "State" from Article 366(26B) clarifies the entities (including certain Union territories) whose governments are referenced in this disqualification clause, thereby delineating the scope of the office of profit disqualification for state legislature membership. Separately, Article 119 grants Parliament the power to regulate by law the procedure in relation to financial business for the timely completion of such business, and such law prevails over inconsistent parliamentary rules. This article establishes Parliament's legislative authority over its own financial procedures, which is a distinct power from the definitional and substantive membership rules covered in Articles 366 and 191. The connection lies in the constitutional structure: Article 366 provides the interpretative key for terms like "State" used in operational articles like Article 191, while Article 119 exemplifies a specific area where Parliament exercises its legislative power, which is separate from the state-level membership rules but part of the broader constitutional framework governing legislative conduct and governance.

(1) The Governor of a State shall, as soon as may be within one year from the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992, and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year, constitute a Finance Commission to review the financial position of the Panchayats and to make recommendations to the Governor as to—
